what_happened: While a retry job (the GitHub-result retry) was building, free disk fell to 2.1 GB. A different job, the held email-check job, still had an 8.1 GB build folder. The cleanup does not reclaim the build folders of held jobs. The the person running Athena deleted that folder by hand. The running job's build alone used 19 GB.
cause: Disk use is not tracked as a budget. Athena keeps the build folders of held jobs indefinitely and its cleanup skips them. Nothing compares the free disk with what the running builds and the kept folders need. When space runs low, only a person can free it, and it is found only when free space is nearly gone.
prevention: Add a disk check that runs before a build starts and again when free space drops below a threshold. It lists the build folders of held jobs with their sizes. Athena then reclaims them automatically (the held job can be rebuilt on resume), or it refuses to start the build and names which folder to free. The held-job reclaim policy should be written down, so that reclaiming a folder never loses work that cannot be rebuilt.
proposed_request: Make Athena's disk cleanup cover the build folders of held jobs. Outcome: when free disk falls below the configured guard threshold, or before a build starts that would take free disk below it, Athena reclaims the build folders of held jobs, oldest first, until enough space is free. It records each reclaimed folder, and a held job whose folder was reclaimed is rebuilt when it resumes. If reclaiming cannot free enough space, Athena stops the new build before it starts and the message names the held folders and their sizes. Acceptance criteria: (1) a test with a held job's build folder present and free disk below the threshold shows the folder is reclaimed and logged; (2) a test shows a held job whose folder was reclaimed still resumes and rebuilds; (3) a test shows the build is refused with a message listing the folder sizes when reclaiming is not enough; (4) the existing cleanup tests still pass.
